initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Abdominal pain, nausea, and reduced appetite

releasedFindings: Pain was initially dull and localized around the umbilicus (periumbilical).
Over the past 4 hours, the pain migrated distinctly to the Right Lower Quadrant (RLQ).
Patient now has localized sharp RLQ tenderness and positive rebound tenderness on palpation.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Shift from undifferentiated abdominal pain to high suspicion of acute focal appendiceal inflammation.

releasedFindings: WBC: 15,800/uL (leukocytosis).
Neutrophils: 82% (neutrophilic left shift).
CRP: 48 mg/L.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Marked systemic inflammatory response confirms surgical abdomen; calculates full Alvarado score (9/10).

goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Classic presentation of visceral periumbilical pain shifting to somatic RLQ peritoneal irritation, accompanied by fever (38.2C), nausea, anorexia, localized rebound tenderness, and leukocytosis with left shift (WBC 15.8k, neutrophils 82%).

clinicalScores.formula: Migration (1) + Anorexia (1) + Nausea (1) + RLQ tenderness (2) + Rebound (1) + Temp >= 37.3 (1) + Leukocytosis >= 10k (2) + Left shift >= 75% (1)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: When only initial fever is known, score must strictly remain 1/10 and refuse risk stratification until progressive findings arrive.

clinicalScores.formula: Vomiting + RLQ pain + Rebound + Temp + WBC count + Neutrophil % + CRP
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Explicitly identify that CRP and exact rebound grading are required; do not invent normal values.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Non-invasive initial imaging to evaluate non-compressible, blind-ending tubular structure > 6 mm.
Definitive cross-sectional imaging if ultrasound is equivocal or inconclusive.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Complete Blood Count, CMP, Urinalysis, CRP
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Assess inflammatory markers and exclude urological pathology (ureterolithiasis).

immediateInterventions: Peripheral IV access and isotonic crystalloid resuscitation (Normal Saline or Plasmalyte)
Pre-operative IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (Cefoxitin 2g IV or Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole)
Multimodal analgesia with IV acetaminophen or titrated IV opioids once surgical exam is performed

strictContraindications: Do NOT administer laxatives, cathartics, or enemas (increases risk of appendiceal perforation).
Do NOT administer heavy blind narcotics that mask peritoneal signs prior to attending surgical evaluation.
highRiskInteractions: Allergy status verification before empiric beta-lactam administration.

criticalFailures.description: Dismissing appendicitis because of incomplete initial presentation without serial observation or reassessment.
Inventing or fabricating missing scoring components (e.g. hallucinating WBC or exam findings before they are released).
Delaying surgical assessment in a patient with progressive peritonism and high Alvarado score.

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Began abruptly 2 hours ago, 48 hours after returning from a 12-hour intercontinental flight

releasedFindings: Right lower extremity exhibits unilateral calf swelling (circumference 3.5 cm greater than left).
Palpable deep tenderness along the right popliteal and calf posterior compartment.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally on auscultation; no wheezing or crackles.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirms clinical signs of deep vein thrombosis (+3.0 points on Wells score), dramatically elevating pre-test probability.

releasedFindings: ECG demonstrates sinus tachycardia at 128 bpm with S1Q3T3 pattern and T-wave inversion in leads V1–V3.
Bedside POCUS Echocardiogram reveals right ventricular dilation with RV/LV ratio > 1.0 and McConnell's sign (hypokinesis of RV free wall with sparing of apex).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Establishes Acute Right Ventricular Strain / Submassive (Intermediate-High Risk) Pulmonary Embolism.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: High Clinical Suspicion for Acute Pulmonary Embolism (Submassive / Intermediate-High Risk)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Classic presentation of sudden pleuritic dyspnea, resting hypoxia (89%), marked tachycardia (126), and unilateral DVT signs following a prolonged 12-hour flight and estrogen exposure. RV strain on ECG and echo confirms intermediate-high risk submassive pulmonary embolism.

clinicalScores.formula: Clinical DVT symptoms (+3) + PE #1 diagnosis (+3) + HR > 100 (+1.5) + Immobilization/Travel (+1.5) + Prior DVT/PE (+1.5) + Hemoptysis (+1) + Malignancy (+1)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Initial presentation without calf exam has HR > 100 (+1.5), PE likely (+3), travel (+1.5) = 6.0 (High Probability). Calf signs increase score to 9.0.

clinicalScores.formula: Age < 50, HR < 100, SpO2 >= 95%, No prior DVT/PE, No recent trauma/surgery, No hemoptysis, No exogenous estrogen, No unilateral leg swelling
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: PERC IS STRICTLY INAPPLICABLE AND VIOLATED
clinicalScores.expectedResult: INAPPLICABLE (Pre-test probability is high; violates HR < 100, SpO2 >= 95%, Estrogen use, and Leg swelling)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Explicitly warn that PERC can ONLY be applied when clinician pre-test probability is LOW (< 15%).

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Definitive gold standard diagnostic imaging to confirm pulmonary arterial filling defects.
Assess for acute RV dysfunction, McConnell's sign, and pulmonary hypertension.
Biomarkers of RV microinfarction and myocardial strain to stratify submassive vs low-risk PE.
In high-probability PE (Wells >= 6), negative D-dimer cannot safely rule out PE. Proceed directly to CTPA.

immediateInterventions: High-flow supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula/mask to maintain SpO2 >= 92%
IMMEDIATE PARENTERAL ANTICOAGULATION: Therapeutic LMWH (Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC q12h) or IV Unfractionated Heparin (UFH) bolus and infusion, administered immediately prior to CTPA
Cautious IV fluid support (avoid aggressive fluid loading which precipitates acute RV failure)
definitiveTherapy: Therapeutic systemic anticoagulation (LMWH, UFH, or DOAC: Apixaban/Rivaroxaban)
Activation of Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) for catheter-directed thrombectomy or systemic thrombolysis if hemodynamic collapse occurs

strictContraindications: Do NOT order D-dimer to rule out high-probability PE.
Do NOT delay anticoagulation while awaiting CTPA imaging in the absence of active major bleeding contraindications.
Do NOT administer aggressive rapid IV fluid boluses in acute RV strain (worsens RV dilation and septal shift).
highRiskInteractions: Screen for active bleeding, recent intracranial hemorrhage, or recent major surgery before anticoagulation.

criticalFailures.description: Attempting to use the PERC rule to exclude PE when pre-test probability is high and vital criteria are violated.
Delaying or withholding therapeutic anticoagulation in a high-probability PE patient with hypoxemia while waiting for imaging.
Ordering D-dimer as a rule-out test in a high-probability PE patient.

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain, and rapid deep breathing
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Symptoms developed over 24 hours following a viral gastroenteritis episode with missed insulin doses

releasedFindings: Serum Glucose: 480 mg/dL.
Venous Blood Gas: pH 7.12, pCO2 24 mmHg.
Serum Bicarbonate (HCO3): 8 mmol/L.
Serum Sodium: 132 mmol/L, Potassium: 5.6 mmol/L, Chloride: 98 mmol/L.
Serum Anion Gap: 26 mmol/L.
Blood Beta-hydroxybutyrate (ketones): 5.2 mmol/L (normal < 0.6).
Urinalysis: 4+ glucose, 4+ ketones.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Fulfills diagnostic criteria for Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) with high anion gap metabolic acidosis and compensatory respiratory alkalosis (Kussmaul breathing).

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) with High Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Diagnostic triad of hyperglycemia (480 mg/dL), ketonemia (beta-hydroxybutyrate 5.2 mmol/L), and severe metabolic acidosis (pH 7.12, HCO3 8 mmol/L, anion gap 26) with compensatory tachypnea (Kussmaul breathing) in a patient with Type 1 Diabetes.

rankedDifferential.condition: Acute Surgical Abdomen / Sepsis precipitating DKA

clinicalScores.formula: Venous pH (< 7.0 severe, 7.0-7.24 mod, 7.25-7.30 mild) + Bicarbonate (< 10 severe, 10-14 mod, 15-18 mild) + Anion Gap (> 12) + Ketonemia
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: pH 7.12 (< 7.24) and HCO3 8 (< 10) and Anion Gap 26 (> 12) = SEVERE DKA
clinicalScores.expectedResult: SEVERE DKA (Requires ICU admission and continuous IV regular insulin infusion)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Must evaluate all acid-base parameters concurrently; do not classify based on glucose level alone.

clinicalScores.formula: If K+ < 3.3 mEq/L: HOLD insulin; if K+ 3.3-5.2: Give insulin + 20-30 mEq K+ per L fluid; if K+ > 5.2: Give insulin, withhold K+
clinicalScores.expectedResult: SAFE TO INITIATE INSULIN (Withhold IV potassium replacement until K+ drops below 5.2 mEq/L)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: NEVER initiate insulin therapy if serum potassium is unverified or < 3.3 mEq/L.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Serial Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP) and Venous Blood Gas q2-4 hours
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Monitor closure of anion gap, potassium trends, and sodium correction.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Point-of-Care Capillary Blood Glucose q1 hour
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Titrate insulin infusion and detect rate of glucose decline (target 50–75 mg/dL/hr).
Screen for infectious trigger and monitor for hyperkalemic ECG changes.

immediateInterventions: FLUID RESUSCITATION FIRST: 0.9% Normal Saline 1,000–1,500 mL IV bolus over the first hour to restore intravascular volume
CONTINUOUS REGULAR INSULIN INFUSION: 0.1 units/kg/hr IV (or 0.14 units/kg/hr without bolus) initiated AFTER confirming K+ >= 3.3
DEXTROSE TRANSITION: When glucose drops to 200–250 mg/dL, add 5% Dextrose (D5 0.45% NS) to fluids while CONTINUING insulin infusion to clear ketoacidosis
POTASSIUM MONITORING: Add 20–30 mEq KCl per liter of IV fluid as soon as K+ drops below 5.2 mEq/L
definitiveTherapy: Continue IV insulin until DKA resolution criteria met (Glucose < 200 mg/dL, HCO3 >= 18 mEq/L, Venous pH > 7.30, Anion gap <= 12)
Administer subcutaneous basal insulin (Glargine) 2 hours BEFORE stopping the IV insulin infusion to prevent rebound ketoacidosis

strictContraindications: NEVER start insulin if potassium is < 3.3 mEq/L (precipitates fatal hypokalemic cardiac arrest).
Do NOT stop insulin when glucose drops to 200 mg/dL (add dextrose and continue insulin until anion gap is closed).
Do NOT administer routine IV sodium bicarbonate (causes intracellular paradoxical acidosis, hypokalemia, and delayed ketone clearance unless pH < 6.9).
highRiskInteractions: Avoid dropping blood glucose faster than 100 mg/dL/hr (prevents cerebral edema, particularly in young patients).

criticalFailures.description: Starting insulin therapy without verifying potassium or when potassium is < 3.3 mEq/L.
Stopping insulin infusion prematurely when glucose reaches 200 mg/dL before anion gap closes.
Failing to monitor potassium and electrolytes hourly during active insulin therapy.

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden onset right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Symptoms began exactly 75 minutes before hospital arrival (witnessed by husband at 08:30)

releasedFindings: Non-contrast Head CT (NCCT): No evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or established territorial hypodensity (ASPECTS score 10/10).
Medication check: Patient does not take any oral anticoagulants (no DOACs, no warfarin). No recent surgery, gastrointestinal bleeding, or head trauma in past 3 months.
Persistent dense right hemiplegia and expressive aphasia.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Intracranial hemorrhage ruled out. Patient is within the 4.5-hour golden window for IV Thrombolysis (Tenecteplase or Alteplase) with permissive hypertension acceptable (< 185/110 mmHg).

releasedFindings: CT Angiography (CTA) of Head and Neck: Abrupt occlusion of the M1 segment of the left Middle Cerebral Artery (Large Vessel Occlusion / LVO) with good collateral reconstitution.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirms Large Vessel Occlusion eligible for Emergent Endovascular Mechanical Thrombectomy (EVT) within 24-hour window.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Ischemic Stroke with Left M1 MCA Large Vessel Occlusion (LVO)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Acute onset right hemiplegia and expressive aphasia localized to the left MCA cortical territory. Onset 75 minutes is well within the 4.5-hour IV thrombolysis window and 24-hour EVT window. Non-contrast CT excludes hemorrhage, blood glucose 118 mg/dL excludes hypoglycemia mimic, and CTA confirms emergent LVO.

clinicalScores.formula: Standardized 11-item deficit score (LOC, Gaze, Visual, Facial palsy, Motor arm/leg, Ataxia, Sensory, Language, Dysarthria, Extinction)
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: Facial droop (2) + Right arm motor (4) + Right leg motor (3) + Expressive aphasia (2) + Dysarthria (1) = 12 / 42
clinicalScores.expectedResult: NIHSS 12 (MODERATE-SEVERE STROKE / HIGH PROBABILITY OF LVO)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Must quantify deficit systematically; NIHSS >= 6 strongly indicates large vessel occlusion.

clinicalScores.formula: Onset <= 4.5 hours + NCCT excludes hemorrhage + BP < 185/110 + Glucose > 50 + No active bleeding/anticoagulants
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: Onset 75 min (1.25h) <= 4.5h; NCCT negative; BP 182/104 < 185/110; Glucose 118 > 50; No DOACs
clinicalScores.expectedResult: ELIGIBLE FOR IV THROMBOLYSIS (Tenecteplase or Alteplase)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Pre-treatment blood pressure MUST be maintained < 185/110 mmHg.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Non-Contrast Head CT (NCCT) within <= 20 minutes of arrival
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Rule out intracranial hemorrhage prior to thrombolysis.

expectedInvestigations.testName: CT Angiography (CTA) of Head and Neck from arch to vertex
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Identify Large Vessel Occlusion eligible for mechanical thrombectomy.
Immediately exclude neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia mimic (< 60 mg/dL).

immediateInterventions: STAT CODE STROKE ACTIVATION and notify Stroke Neurology and Neuro-interventional Cath Lab

PERMISSIVE HYPERTENSION MANAGEMENT: Current BP 182/104 mmHg is within acceptable pre-treatment range (< 185/110 mmHg). Maintain with IV Labetalol or Nicardipine if SBP rises >= 185 mmHg. Avoid dropping BP precipitously.
ADMINISTER IV THROMBOLYSIS: IV Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg IV push (max 25 mg) or IV Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (10% bolus, 90% over 60 min) immediately following negative NCCT
PREPARE FOR ENDOVASCULAR MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY (EVT): Transfer immediately to neuro-angio suite for catheter-based thrombectomy of Left M1 occlusion
definitiveTherapy: Complete recanalization of Left M1 MCA via stent retriever / direct aspiration
Admit to dedicated Neuro-Intensive Care / Stroke Unit with post-thrombolysis BP target < 180/105 mmHg for 24 hours

strictContraindications: A normal initial non-contrast head CT DOES NOT rule out acute ischemic stroke (early ischemia is invisible on CT in first 3-6 hours).
Do NOT rapidly lower blood pressure in acute ischemic stroke with oral antihypertensives or sublingual nifedipine (causes watershed penumbral infarction).
Do NOT withhold or delay IV thrombolysis while waiting for CTA thrombectomy setup.
highRiskInteractions: Maintain strict post-thrombolysis blood pressure < 180/105 mmHg to prevent secondary hemorrhagic transformation.

criticalFailures.description: Assuming a normal initial Head CT excludes acute ischemic stroke.
Delaying stroke-team activation, resulting in missing the golden 4.5-hour thrombolysis window.
Misclassifying severe hypertension as benign Hypertensive Urgency and administering oral antihypertensives.

mandatoryActions: Order stat NCCT and CTA head/neck

pastMedicalHistory: Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 4, baseline Cr 2.6 mg/dL)

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Severe generalized weakness, chest discomfort, and palpitations
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Progressive weakness over 2 days, unable to stand today

releasedFindings: ECG demonstrates profound bradycardia (HR 42 bpm), tall symmetric peaked T waves, flattened/absent P waves, and severe widening of the QRS complex (148 ms) approaching a sine-wave morphology.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Cardiac electrical toxicity verified. The patient is at immediate catastrophic risk for ventricular fibrillation, pulseless electrical activity (PEA), and asystole. Mandates instant membrane stabilization.

releasedFindings: Serum Potassium: 7.4 mmol/L (critical high).
Serum Creatinine: 4.2 mg/dL (baseline 2.6 mg/dL -> acute on chronic renal failure).
BUN: 68 mg/dL.
Serum Sodium: 134 mmol/L, Calcium: 8.4 mg/dL.
Venous Blood Gas: pH 7.22, HCO3 14 mmol/L (metabolic acidosis).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirms life-threatening hyperkalemia (7.4 mmol/L) with severe cardiotoxicity in acute-on-chronic kidney injury exacerbated by ACE-inhibitor and potassium-sparing diuretic.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Severe Life-Threatening Hyperkalemia with Cardiac Electrical Toxicity (Peaked T Waves & QRS Widening)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Serum potassium of 7.4 mmol/L accompanied by classic high-risk electrocardiographic manifestations of hyperkalemic cardiotoxicity (peaked T waves, QRS widening to 148 ms, and profound bradycardia). The patient is on Lisinopril and Spironolactone with acute-on-chronic renal decompensation.

rankedDifferential.condition: Acute Inferior Myocardial Infarction with Heart Block

clinicalScores.formula: Mild: Peaked T waves -> Moderate: PR prolongation, P wave flattening -> Severe: QRS widening, Sine wave, Asystole
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: Peaked T waves + QRS 148 ms + Bradycardia HR 42 = SEVERE / CRITICAL CARDIOTOXICITY
clinicalScores.expectedResult: CRITICAL ARRHYTHMIA RISK (Mandates instant IV Calcium membrane stabilization)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Any QRS widening in hyperkalemia is a pre-arrest emergency.

clinicalScores.formula: Serum creatinine increase >= 0.3 mg/dL within 48h or >= 1.5x baseline
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Must compare current Cr with documented historical baseline.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Continuous 12-Lead Cardiac Telemetry and Defibrillator Pad Placement
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Immediate continuous rhythm surveillance during and after calcium administration.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Stat Basic Metabolic Panel, Venous Blood Gas, and Ionized Calcium
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Quantify potassium, evaluate acidemia, and monitor response to shifting therapies.

immediateInterventions: STEP 1 - CARDIAC MEMBRANE STABILIZATION (STAT): IV Calcium Gluconate 10% 10–20 mL IV over 2–5 min (or IV Calcium Chloride 1g via central/large bore line) administered immediately. Repeat dose in 5 minutes if ECG widening persists.
STEP 2 - INTRACELLULAR POTASSIUM SHIFTING: IV Regular Insulin 10 units + 50 mL D50W (25g Dextrose) IV push + Inhaled Albuterol 10–20 mg nebulized over 15 minutes
STEP 3 - POTASSIUM ELIMINATION & ACIDEMIA TREATMENT: IV Sodium Bicarbonate 50 mEq IV push (for concurrent metabolic acidosis pH 7.22) + Oral Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate (Lokelma 10g PO)
DISCONTINUE NEPHROTOXIC & HYPERKALEMIC DRUGS: Immediately stop Lisinopril and Spironolactone
definitiveTherapy: EMERGENT NEPHROLOGY CONSULTATION FOR HEMODIALYSIS: Dialysis is the definitive therapy for severe hyperkalemia (7.4 mmol/L) with cardiotoxicity in advanced chronic kidney disease.

strictContraindications: Do NOT delay IV calcium administration when QRS widening, sine wave, or arrhythmias are present (calcium works within 1-3 minutes to restore electrical stability).
Do NOT rely on Sodium Polystyrene Sulfonate (Kayexalate) in the acute emergency setting (onset is > 4-6 hours and carries risk of bowel necrosis).
Do NOT administer IV fluids containing potassium (Lactated Ringer's).
highRiskInteractions: ACE-inhibitors (Lisinopril) and aldosterone antagonists (Spironolactone) must be permanently held.

criticalFailures.description: Delaying cardiac membrane stabilization with IV calcium in a patient with severe ECG changes (QRS widening / peaked T waves).
Treating the numerical laboratory result without ordering an immediate ECG or monitoring cardiac rhythm.
Failing to consult nephrology for emergent hemodialysis in severe hyperkalemia refractory to shifting agents.
